bindings.label: 19-year-old female presented with left-sided chest pain and cough, then six weeks later had right lateral chest wall pain, shortness of breath, and menorrhagia after starting rivaroxaban

Initial presentation: 19-year-old female presented to emergency room with left-sided chest pain and cough; CT imaging identified multiple pulmonary emboli in the left inferior segmental pulmonary arteries; no provoking factors or other complications at that time; discharged on rivaroxaban with hemoglobin 14.9 g/dL and platelet count 402 per uL.

Six weeks later, she returned with right lateral chest wall pain and shortness of breath; hemoglobin 6.6 g/dL, platelet count 485 per uL; she reported developing menorrhagia after starting rivaroxaban.

Follow-up CT imaging showed a new pulmonary embolism in the right lower lobe segmental pulmonary arteries and decreased clot burden in the left inferior segmental pulmonary artery branches; she received packed red blood cell transfusion and was started on heparin drip; no signs of heart failure or hypoxia; started on norethindrone for menses suppression.

Laboratory tests showed ferritin 6.8 ng/mL and she received an iron transfusion; she was transitioned to warfarin; one month later hemoglobin 10.8 g/dL, ferritin 36.1 ng/mL, iron saturation 25%, and platelet count 566 per uL.

Hypercoagulable workup including protein C, protein S, antithrombin III, factor V Leiden, prothrombin gene mutations, lupus anticoagulant, cardiolipin antibodies, and beta-2 glycoprotein antibodies was unrevealing; testing for JAK2, MPL, CALR, and JAK2 exon 12-15 mutations was negative; subsequent CSA revealed heterozygous variant of unknown significance Chr1(GRCh37):g.43805172C>A predicted to result in glutamine to lysine substitution at codon 208 in exon 4 of MPL gene, not reported as associated with a clinical condition according to HGMD; father was being treated for a similar condition.
Bone marrow biopsy shows normocellular marrow with mild megakaryocytic hyperplasia and no dysplasia
